note: Window agent corrections, 2 Nov 2026: Ireland restored to its kingdom (lost in the 1660s), Haudenosaunee homeland kept from the thirteen colonies, Kamchatka kept by Russia, Kandahar kept by the Safavids (Mughal 1709 shape without it), Kolhapur kept in the Maratha realm until 1710, Bono kept until 1722.

events.note: 1700: the whole island is the Crown's Kingdom of Ireland. 'The conquest of the island was completed early in the 17th century' and 'the whole island was brought under the centralised control of an Anglo-centric system based in Dublin'; the kingdom 'was a dependency of England from 1542 to 1707, and then of Great Britain from 1707 to 1800'. The draft holds 278 of the island's 344 cells as nobody's from 1662 (commonwealth-of-england/ledger/16 passes them to kingdom-of-england in 1660 and kingdom-of-england_1662 releases them); this restores the land of the kingdom's own 1660-1800 keyframe.

region.text: the Haudenosaunee homeland in central and western New York and northern Pennsylvania (the 1702 shape)

events.note: 1700: the homeland is the Confederacy's. 'The Iroquois preserved considerable independence' and remained 'a large politically united Native American polity until the' American Revolution; 'until 1707, treaties were between the' Five Nations and England (treaty partners, not subjects). The draft gives 273 of the 282 homeland cells to the thirteen colonies (colony rule R1 in the keyframe conflict).

correction.text: the 1706 shape with the whole province of Kandahar

keyframe_overrides.why: 'The Shi'a Safavids ruled Loy Kandahar as their easternmost territory from the 16th century until the early 18th century'; Shah Husayn appointed Gurgin Khan governor of Kandahar in 1704. The Cliopatria 1706 shape moves 74 Kandahar cells out of the Safavid land (into its Mughal row), so the draft leaves them nobody's in 1706-1708 and the Mughal 1709 keyframe then takes them; the page names no Mughal rule there in 1700-1709.

correction.text: the 1709 shape with the whole province of Kandahar, without the Kandahar oasis the Hotaki hold from 21 April 1709

keyframe_overrides.why: Mirwais Hotak's revolt of 21 April 1709 took the Kandahar oasis ('expelled the Georgian garrison from Kandahar'); only later 'Mirwais was able to extend his control over the entire province of Kandahar' (after the Persian commander died, 1712; ledger hotaki-dynasty/3). Until then the rest of the province stays Safavid; the draft hands 74 of its cells to the Mughal Empire.

correction.text: Shahu's Satara core plus Tarabai's Kolhapur seat, which stays inside the Maratha realm until the Kolhapur state is founded in 1710

keyframe_overrides.why: The page has 'two rival seats of government being set up in 1707 at Satara and Kolhapur' inside the one Maratha realm; the kolhapur-state dossier begins only in 1710 (ledger found maratha-empire), so ledger maratha-empire/11 (split, 1707) leaves the 33 Kolhapur cells nobody's for three years and the Mughal 1709 keyframe then takes them. Kolhapur stays Maratha until the founding.

The draft hands the 74 cells to the Mughals in 1709.

correction.text: Bonoman, the Brong country, independent until the Asante conquest of 1722-1723

keyframe_overrides.why: 'Asante invaded Bono in 1722-1723' and 'Bono was defeated in 1723, ending its independence' (infobox 1723): Bono stayed independent through 1701-1721. The draft empties the state in 1701: ashanti-empire/ledger/0 takes 34 Brong Ahafo cells and the ashanti-empire_1701 snap releases 131 more to nobody, so Bono holds no land from 1701 to 1722. The new keyframe is the dossier's own bono-state_1450 shape (Brong Ahafo) re-applied from 1701; the 34 cells in Ashanti's own 1702 shape stay Ashanti's.
